In my experience, you should try to increase the download speed as much as possible. 

Using a downloader that allows proxy configuration, supports multi-threading, file splitting and resumable downloads may help.

On Linux, I use `uGet` as the downloader and configure the plugin to be `aria2 + curl`. `uGet` is basically ready to use out of the box. The main thing is to configure `aria2`. There are many tutorials on how to configure `aria2c` on the Internet.

If configured correctly, downloading the same file using uGet may be 4x faster than using the default downloader in Firefox/Chromium browsers.

I can confirm the following script works well on Linux Mint and probably Ubuntu and more. It will resume the download after the GH token expires. It also keeps a log. 
https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/169381#discussioncomment-14103622

```
#!/bin/bash
export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8
counter=1
until wget -o ./log$counter.txt -c https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/download/4.4.1-stable/Godot_v4.4.1-stable_export_templates.tpz
do
((counter++))
done
```

Copy this text in to a text editor. Change the URL to one you like and need. Save as `your-name.sh` . Change the permissions of this file to allow it to be run as an application. Run the script.

It will run in the background as a wget process and download the file. The file will be located in the same directory as the script file.

> wget works differently in Windows, please check the documentation

To clarify, @Serimert90 needs to call `wget` as `wget.exe` (same for `curl` - it should be `curl.exe`). Otherwise, it calls PowerShell's alias for `Invoke-WebRequest` (which has its own `iwr` alias, should you want to use it).

Explicitly mentioning `wget.exe`/`curl.exe` is only needed in PowerShell (not on cmd), but it's a good idea to always do it for consistent behavior across shells.

I can confirm the speculation stated elsewhere: it is a timing problem. After a fixed period of time, GitHub stops the download.

So, you need a connection fast enough to download the full file before GitHub stops the download.

OR, if you drop to command line, you can use the GNU utility called `wget` to get around that. On Fedora, simply run `sudo dnf install wget -y` to download the utility if you don't have it. Simply run 

```bash
wget -c https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/4.5-dev4/Godot_v4.5-dev4_mono_export_templates.tpz
```

_(or use whatever url you need)_ When the  download stops, simply run the `wget` command again with the `-c` option to pickup where you left off. It took me two tries but it worked.
